b: \( \tfrac{d}{dx}e^{x}=e^{x} \), \( \tfrac{d}{dx}\ln x=\tfrac1x \), \( \tfrac{d}{dx}\sin x=\cos x \). Chain: \( \tfrac{dy}{dx}=\tfrac{dy}{du}\tfrac{du}{dx} \). Product: \( (uv)'=u'v+uv' \). Quotient: \( \left(\tfrac{u}{v}\right)'=\dfrac{u'v-uv'}{v^{2}} \).

b: Local Linearization & Differentiability: A function \(f\) is differentiable at \(x = a\) if and only if the difference quotient \(\lim_{h \to 0} \dfrac{f(a+h) - f(a)}{h}\) exists as a finite real number. Differentiability at \(x = a\) strictly implies continuity at \(x = a\), but the converse fails at sharp corners (e.g. \(|x - 4|\)), vertical tangents, or jump discontinuities.

b: \( \displaystyle\int x^{n}\,dx=\dfrac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}+C \) (\( n\neq-1 \)); \( \displaystyle\int e^{x}\,dx=e^{x}+C \); \( \displaystyle\int\tfrac1x\,dx=\ln|x|+C \). A definite integral gives the signed area: \( F(b)-F(a) \).

b: Accumulation, Antiderivatives & Differential Flows: By the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, the accumulation function \(A(x) = \int_a^x f(t)\,dt\) satisfies \(A'(x) = f(x)\), linking instantaneous rates of change to net signed area. In first-order differential equations \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = g(x)h(y)\), separation of variables \(\int \dfrac{1}{h(y)}\,dy = \int g(x)\,dx + C\) reconstructs the family of integral curves across the slope field.
